title: Mandarin Connect: Count and write
_note: say = text sent to ElevenLabs (Chinese characters where Mandarin must be pronounced); cap = on-screen caption (pinyin).

lines.say: 你好！
lines.cap: Nǐ hǎo!

lines.say: Hello! Today we learn two things: how to count, and how to write. In Chinese!
lines.cap: Hello! Today we learn two things: how to count, and how to write. In Chinese!

lines.say: Count and write. Mandarin for beginners. 我们开始吧！
lines.cap: Count and write. Mandarin for beginners. Wǒmen kāishǐ ba: let’s begin!

lines.say: First, numbers. Say them with me.
lines.cap: First, numbers. Say them with me.

lines.say: 一，二，三，四，五。
lines.cap: Yī, èr, sān, sì, wǔ.

lines.say: One, two, three, four, five. Easy!
lines.cap: One, two, three, four, five. Easy!

lines.say: 六，七，八，九，十。
lines.cap: Liù, qī, bā, jiǔ, shí.

lines.say: Six to ten. And look: one, two and three are just lines!
lines.cap: Six to ten. And look: one, two and three are just lines!

lines.say: Yes! One line for one, two lines for two, three lines for three.
lines.cap: Yes! One line for one, two lines for two, three lines for three.

lines.say: So why is the eight gold?
lines.cap: So why is the eight gold?

lines.say: 八 is a lucky number in China. It sounds like 发, which means to prosper.
lines.cap: Bā is a lucky number in China. It sounds like fā, which means to prosper.

lines.say: Now a secret. Chinese numbers are building blocks.
lines.cap: Now a secret. Chinese numbers are building blocks.

lines.say: Ten and one: 十一. Eleven.
lines.cap: Ten and one: shíyī. Eleven.

lines.say: Two tens: 二十. Twenty.
lines.cap: Two tens: èrshí. Twenty.

lines.say: Wait. So ninety-nine is nine, ten, nine?
lines.cap: Wait. So ninety-nine is nine, ten, nine?

lines.say: Exactly! 九十九.
lines.cap: Exactly! Jiǔshíjiǔ.

lines.say: Quick quiz! Three plus five. In Chinese?
lines.cap: Quick quiz! Three plus five. In Chinese?

lines.say: 八！ Eight. The lucky one.
lines.cap: Bā! Eight. The lucky one.

lines.say: Numbers, done. Now, writing. Are Chinese characters just pictures?
lines.cap: Numbers, done. Now, writing. Are Chinese characters just pictures?

lines.say: Many began as pictures, carved on bones and shells more than three thousand years ago.
lines.cap: Many began as pictures, carved on bones and shells more than three thousand years ago.

lines.say: 人. A person, walking.
lines.cap: Rén. A person, walking.

lines.say: 山. Three mountain peaks.
lines.cap: Shān. Three mountain peaks.

lines.say: 日. The sun. It also means a day.
lines.cap: Rì. The sun. It also means a day.

lines.say: 木. A tree, with its roots.
lines.cap: Mù. A tree, with its roots.

lines.say: So what happens if I write two trees?
lines.cap: So what happens if I write two trees?

lines.say: Two trees: 林, the woods. Three trees: 森, a forest!
lines.cap: Two trees: lín, the woods. Three trees: sēn, a forest!

lines.say: That's genius. I can read a forest!
lines.cap: That’s genius. I can read a forest!

lines.say: Now, write your first character. 中. It means middle.
lines.cap: Now, write your first character. Zhōng. It means middle.

lines.say: Four strokes. Down. Across, and down. Along the bottom. And the long line, last.
lines.cap: Four strokes. Down. Across, and down. Along the bottom. And the long line, last.

lines.say: And 中国 is China: the Middle Kingdom.
lines.cap: And Zhōngguó is China: the Middle Kingdom.

lines.say: Practise every day, and say it out loud. 加油！
lines.cap: Practise every day, and say it out loud. Jiāyóu: you can do it!

lines.say: Mandarin Connect, at Royal Crest Academy. 再见！
lines.cap: Mandarin Connect, at Royal Crest Academy. Zàijiàn!

lines.say: 再见！
lines.cap: Zàijiàn!
